headline: Treasury spreads widen to +0.88 and return to Normal
lede: Treasury spreads read +0.88 on October 19, optimistic and back to Normal. The US 10-year Treasury stands at 5.15%, against a Fed range of 3.75–4.00%.
story: Born out of the 2022 correction, the AI Cycle rode the build-out of artificial intelligence, the story everyone wanted to own. It is a market priced for a boom inside an economy that feels like a slowdown: her valuations sit at the top of the record while her people’s confidence sits at the bottom of it, and the distance between the two is the story of this cycle so far.

elements.weather: Autumn, the stagflation kind. [Temperature](sheet-metric-temp) reads hot at 3.4% and is still heating, at Attention, while the [Growth gap](sheet-sign-growth-gap) puts output a shade under its potential. The [Federal funds rate](sheet-sign-hormones) is tightening: the Fed raised a quarter point on September 16, to 3.75–4.00%, and meets again on October 28. The [S&P 500](sheet-sign-market) is in a bull year, up 14.4%.
elements.activity: The body is doing more with few new hands. [GDP growth](sheet-metric-gdp) runs at 2.1% and [Productivity growth](sheet-sign-productivity-growth) is above trend at 2.2%, while [Job growth](sheet-sign-payrolls) is adding jobs at a slow 0.3%, at Attention. The [Unemployment rate](sheet-sign-activity) holds solid at 4.1%.
elements.mood: The split at the centre of this cycle holds. The [Buffett indicator](sheet-metric-buffett) stands at 256%, the highest on its record, at Risk, and [Shiller CAPE](sheet-metric-valuation) reads rich at 40.7×, at Attention, yet [Fear](sheet-sign-sentiment) is calm at 20.0. Households read it the other way: [Confidence](sheet-sign-confidence) is pessimistic at 96.1, at Attention.
elements.desire: Shoppers keep spending: [Discretionary spending](sheet-sign-desire) shows a high appetite at +4.6% and [Retail sales](sheet-sign-retail) are up 5.4%, while [Consumer credit](sheet-sign-consumer-credit) is borrowing more, up 2.7%, at Attention. The ten largest stocks make up 40.6% of the S&P 500, a concentrated index by its [Concentration risk](sheet-sign-concentration), and the [Equity risk premium](sheet-sign-premium) is thin at +0.6%, at Attention. [Default risk](sheet-metric-delinquency) stays below average, at 1.42%.
elements.circulation: The bond market steadied. [Treasury spreads](sheet-sign-spreads) read optimistic at +0.88, back to Normal, as the [US 10-year Treasury](sheet-sign-pressure) stands at 5.15% on October 19 and the [30-year mortgage rate](sheet-sign-mortgage) is rising, at 7.34%. Money still turns slowly: the [Pulse](sheet-sign-pulse) is very slow, at Attention, while [Volume](sheet-sign-volume) holds steady.
elements.stress: Households carry little debt against their income: the [Debt-to-income ratio](sheet-metric-debt-payments) is below average at 11.1%. Their cushion is thin, with the [Savings rate](sheet-sign-saving) at 2.8%, saving very little, at Attention, and investors are borrowing more, with [Margin debt](sheet-sign-margin) at +37%. The heavier load is the state’s: [Federal debt](sheet-metric-debt) is elevated at 122.6%, at Attention, and the [Federal budget](sheet-marker-deficit) runs a large deficit of 5.8% while the economy is still growing.
